name: Mountain Pose
description: The foundational standing posture that teaches grounded stability, opens the chest, and aligns skeletal posture.
instructions: Stand with bases of big toes touching, heels slightly apart.
Lift and fan out your toes, then lay them softly on the mat.
Firm your thigh muscles and lift knee caps without locking joints.
Elongate your spine and roll shoulders back and down with arms at sides.
Breathe deeply and smoothly, feeling grounded like a mountain.

name: Tree Pose
description: Cultivates deep concentration, ankle stability, and hip opening while calming neurological hyperactivity.
benefits: Enhances equilibrium and nervous system balance
instructions: Begin in Mountain Pose, shifting weight onto left foot.
Bend right knee and place right foot sole on inner left thigh or calf.
Find an unmoving focal point (drishti) at eye level.
Bring hands together in Anjali Mudra (prayer pose) at heart center or overhead.
Hold for 5-10 deep breaths, then switch sides.

name: Cobra Pose
description: Gentle prone backbend that strengthens the spine, stimulates abdominal kidneys, and relieves mild fatigue.
benefits: Expands lung capacity and relieves mild asthma
instructions: Lie prone on your belly with legs extended and tops of feet flat.
Place palms under shoulders, hugging elbows close to torso.
Inhale and slowly lift chest off floor, engaging back muscles.
Keep shoulders dropped away from ears and gaze softly forward.
Exhale and slowly lower chest back down to the floor.

name: Child's Pose
description: A deeply restorative sanctuary posture that gently releases back tension and soothes stress and anxiety.
benefits: Gently stretches hips, thighs, and ankles
instructions: Kneel on the floor, bring big toes together, separate knees hip-width.
Exhale and fold torso down between thighs.
Rest forehead gently onto mat or yoga block.
Extend arms forward along floor or alongside thighs.
Breathe deeply into lower back and ribs.

name: Downward-Facing Dog
description: Rejuvenating full-body stretch that energizes the nervous system while strengthening hamstrings, shoulders, and wrists.
benefits: Calms the brain and relieves mild fatigue
instructions: Come onto hands and knees in tabletop position.
Tuck toes, press firmly through palms, lift knees away from floor.
Lift sitting bones high toward ceiling and lengthen spine.
Keep knees slightly bent if hamstrings feel tight.
Relax head between upper arms and take 5 deep cycles of breath.

name: Easy Pose
description: A peaceful seated meditation posture that promotes an erect spine, relaxed hips, and calm rhythmic breath.
benefits: Optimal posture for pranayama and meditation
instructions: Sit comfortably cross-legged on the floor or on a folded blanket.
Align head, neck, and spine directly over pelvis.
Rest hands on knees with palms facing down or up.
Close eyes softly and relax facial and jaw muscles.
Focus gently on the steady natural flow of your breathing.
